intent: Someone searching for artificial turf in Denver, including the Berkley pocket of unincorporated Adams County that borders the city, should land on one page that tells them which authority and which water provider actually govern their address.
distinctValue: Old Denver's fill-over-clay ground, its Stage 1 drought rules with no turf rebate, and Berkley's split between two water districts that both answer to Denver Water while sitting outside city jurisdiction for permits.

sources.label: Berkeley Water and Sanitation District
supports: The District boundaries are from the north side of 52nd Avenue to 60th Avenue from Sheridan Boulevard to Tejon Street.
As of January 1, 2018, Denver Water will provide all water services.

sources.label: Crestview Water and Sanitation District: boundary map
supports: They are roughly, Tennyson Street on the west to I-25 on the east then 56th avenue on the south to Sherrylwood Lane on the north.
For all of the Denver Water/Crestview Water restrictions, please visit our drought page to view the Denver Water Restrictions Resolution.

sources.label: Crestmoor Park (2nd Filing) Homes Association Design Guidelines
supports: Originally Adopted April 13, 2011 / Revision Adopted May 6, 2024 / Revision Adopted May 19, 2026

BEFORE COMMENCING ANY DEVELOPMENT OF OR EXTERIOR IMPROVEMENT TO PROPERTY WITHIN THE CRESTMOOR PARK (2ND FILING) COMMUNITY, YOU MUST OBTAIN APPROVAL OF THE PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT FROM THE ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW COMMITTEE ("ARC") OF THE CRESTMOOR PARK (2ND FILING) HOMES ASSOCIATION

Development includes, without limitation ... (3) the grading, excavation, filling, or similar disturbance to the surface of the land, including, without limitation, landscaping, change of grade, change of ground level, or change of drainage pattern
Homes located on corner lots will have two front Setbacks (one on each street side of the Home) and two side Setbacks of eight (8) feet each.

No Development other than landscaping shall be installed in any Setback except for: A. Subsurface structures ... B. Steps, driveways ... C. Underground utilities ... D. Fences, only in side and rear Setbacks ... E. Certain permitted encroachments ... F. "Little Libraries" ... G. "Garden Landscape Walls"

Section 1.32, Artificial Turf: Although not encouraged, premium artificial landscape turf will be accepted with the appropriate submittal. A full specification and sample of the turf must be submitted and approved by the ARC. Only plush rolled goods with a natural, life-like appearance will be considered. Interlocking turf squares are strictly forbidden.

sources.label: Denver Landmark Guidelines: Site & Landscape Design (chapter 5)
supports: 01-27-16 — DENVER, COLORADO (the document's footer date, i.e. January 27, 2016); denvergov.org refused direct connections 13-14 Sept 2026, read via a web.archive.org copy of the same denvergov.org file
5.4 Maintain front yard landscape areas.
a. Reserve most of the front yard area for a grass lawn or a designed xeriscape that uses low-water plantings while maintaining the appearance of a landscaped front yard.
d. Avoid introducing topographic features, such as berms, that were not historically present, especially if other front yard areas on the street do not include similar features.
The guidelines for a “front yard” also apply to a street-facing side yard on a corner property, or other yard areas between buildings and the street.
